Consult Summary:
30-year-old female nurse with 7-day history of fever, night sweats, myalgia, and nausea after travel to rural Vietnam 4 weeks ago; no obvious localising symptoms. Plan for urgent in-person assessment and blood tests including malaria screen.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Fever of unknown origin
- Onset: 7 days ago; intermittent hot/cold episodes and night sweats.
- Associated symptoms: generalised muscle aches, nausea with reduced oral intake, fatigue. OTC ibuprofen/paracetamol give partial relief.
- Review of systems: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhoea, neck stiffness, new/worse headache, rash, joint swelling, dysuria or urinary frequency.
- No home temperature readings documented.

Issue 2: Recent travel–related infection risk
- Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; rural trekking, cycling, river/beach exposure.
- Took daily malaria prophylaxis (exact agent unknown; possible additional tablet).
- Differential: malaria, other tropical infections (e.g., dengue, typhoid, leptospirosis).

Issue 3: Chronic mechanical back pain
- Long-standing; related to prolonged sitting and poor posture.
- Under physiotherapy; focus on posture correction and strengthening exercises.

Medications:
- Paroxetine (Seroxat) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen – OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol – OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Pollen (hay fever). No drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain.

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse.
- Smoking: Never smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake (exact units not documented).
- Exercise: Moderate activity several times per week.
- Vaccinations: Up to date for occupational requirements (incl. Hepatitis B).

Preventative History:
- No information on cervical screening, mammogram, FOBT, BMD, skin or eye checks.

Physical Examination:
- No examination performed during teleconsultation; no vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Urgent face-to-face appointment in central clinic today (admin team to book).
- Physical examination on arrival.
- Laboratory tests to be ordered:
  • Thick & thin blood films for malaria.  
  • Full blood count, renal & liver profile, inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP/ESR).  
  • Additional travel-related infectious screens per clinician review.
- Consider local Emergency Department if unable to attend clinic.
- Advise patient not to attend work until assessment completed.
- Provide clinic contact number in consultation notes for patient to arrange booking.
- Follow-up: results review and further management once investigations available.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: vitals, full medication list with doses, drug allergy confirmation, comprehensive vaccination and screening history.  
● No internal conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality acceptable; minor background conversation but clinically clear.
